tr: Where's the key? / It's on the table, next to the phone.
Shall we get some ice cream? / Yes, I'd love to! I'll have chocolate.
I don't sleep well at night. / Why? Is it too hot?
Do you want sugar in your coffee? / No, thanks, I take it without.
Hi, Luca! How are you? / Great! And you?
Good evening, Mr. Rossi. How are you? / Fine, thank you. And you?
This is my friend Matteo. / Nice to meet you, Matteo!
Thanks a lot for the help! / Don't mention it!
Hi! What's your name? / My name is Giorgia, and you?
Good morning, what's your name? / My name is Paolo Bianchi.
Where are you from, Megan? / I'm American, but now I live in Florence.
Do you speak English? / Yes, a little. But let's speak Italian!
Where do you live now? / I live in Bologna, near the university.
Do you have any brothers or sisters? / Yes, I have a brother and two sisters.
Where do your parents live? / My parents live in Naples.
How's Grandma? / She's well, thanks. On Sunday we're having lunch at her place.
Who's that guy? / That's my boyfriend, Simone.
Sorry, what time is it? / It's ten after five.
How much is this bag? / It's forty euros.
Is it one o'clock already? / Yes, let's go to lunch!
Can I have your phone number? / Sure, I'll write it down for you.
What's the weather like in Milan? / It's raining today, but tomorrow it'll be sunny.
What day is it today? / Today is Thursday.
When is your birthday? / My birthday is March 3.
See you on Monday? / Yes, Monday at ten.
What are you having? / An espresso, thanks.
Would you like something to drink? / A glass of water, please.
Good evening, a table for two? / Yes, this way, please.
And for you, sir? / I'll have the spaghetti with tomato sauce.
What size do you wear? / I wear a 42.
Good morning, can I help you? / I'm just looking, thanks.
This jacket is really nice. Can I try it on? / Of course, the fitting rooms are over there.
How does it look on me? / It looks great on you!
What time do you wake up in the morning? / I wake up at six thirty.
Do you get up early? / Pretty early: I get up at seven.
Do you live in a house? / No, I live in an apartment downtown.
Sorry, where's the bathroom? / At the end of the hall, on the right.
Where is the station? / Go straight and then turn right.
Is the cathedral far? / No, it's five minutes on foot.
Is there a pharmacy near here? / Yes, there's one in the square.
I'm lost. Where are we? / We're near the Colosseum.
What time does the train to Bologna leave? / At 6:20 p.m., from platform three.
One way or round trip? / Round trip, please.
Why are we still waiting? / The train is twenty minutes late.
Good evening. I have a reservation for two nights. / Great. May I see some ID, please?
What's wrong? / I've had a headache since this morning.
Good morning, do you have something for a cough? / Yes, this syrup is very good.
Where does it hurt? / Here, in my knee.
Are you allergic to any medicine? / Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin.
What do you do for work? / I'm a teacher at a middle school.
Are you going to the office today? / No, on Fridays I work from home.
Shall we go out tonight? / I can't, I have an exam tomorrow.
What time do you finish today? / I finish at six, then I'm going home.
I'm hungry. Shall we eat something? / Yes, let's go to a pizzeria.
How are you? / I'm tired, I worked all day.
It's cold, take your jacket. / You're right, thanks.
On Saturday we're going to Venice. / How nice! I can't wait!
Do you like to dance? / Yes, a lot! What about you?
I really like gelato. / Me too!
What did you do on the weekend? / We went to the beach with the kids.
Roma is playing tonight. Shall we watch the game? / Sure, I'll come over to your place at nine.
Who is it? / It's me, Luca!
How old are you? / I'm twenty-eight.
I'm not coming to the party. / Why?
Tea or coffee? / Coffee, thanks.
I'm tired. / Me too. Shall we go home?
Do you know Marco? / Yes, we work together.
Excuse me, can I take a picture? / Yes, but no flash.
Let's take the eight o'clock train, so we get there earlier. / Yes, that makes sense.
Can you swim? / Yes, but not very well.
Good morning, what can I get you? / I'd like a cappuccino and a croissant.
Anything else? / No, thank you. Could you bring me the check?
Good evening, a table for two? / Of course. Please, have a seat.
And you, what will you have? / The lasagna for me.
Thanks for dinner, everything was delicious. / I'm so glad! Would you like a coffee?
I finished the marathon! / Well done!
Shall we go to the beach on Sunday? / Great idea!
I'll help you with the bags. / Thanks, you're very kind.
What a lovely home! / Thanks, that's so kind of you!
What do you think of this dress? / It looks great on you!
You speak Italian very well! / Thanks, but I still have a lot to learn.
I made this cake myself. / You're really good at this!
It smells wonderful! What are you cooking? / Grandma's sauce!
Do you like the risotto? / Yes, it's so good!
Your Italian is perfect! / You think so? I still have a lot to learn.
You're a really good dancer! / Oh, come on, thanks!
You look great today! / Thanks, you too!
This tiramisu is delicious! / Thanks! It's my grandma's recipe.
Are you American? Your pronunciation is excellent! / Thanks a lot, I study a lot.
Do you like my new jacket? / Yes, you have really good taste!
I really like your garden. / Thanks, I'm glad you think so!
You have a nice smile. / Thanks, that's sweet!
You look beautiful tonight. / Thanks! You look great too.
You have gorgeous eyes. / Thanks, they're my mother's eyes.
Why are you laughing? / Because you make me laugh!
I like talking with you. / Me too. Shall we have another espresso?
Do you feel like getting a coffee? / Sure! I know a café near here.
Would you like to go out with me on Saturday? / Yes! Where shall we go?
Are you free Saturday night? / Sorry, I'm working on Saturday.
Will you give me your number? / Sure, here it is.
Can I ask you a question? Are you seeing someone? / No, I'm single. Why?
I have to tell you something: I like you. / I like you too.
I missed you! / I missed you too! How did the trip go?
Will you come to dinner at my place tomorrow? / I'd love to! What time?
Can I walk you home? / I'd really like that.
You're the most beautiful girl at the party. / Do you say that to all the girls?
You're the nicest person in the world! / You're exaggerating!
Please, after you. / How gallant!
I like you, you know? / Same here!
Can I buy you a drink? / Thanks, but I'm seeing someone.
Would you like to go out with me, just the two of us? / You're very sweet, but I'd rather we stayed friends.
Shall we go dancing tonight? / That's kind of you, but no, thanks. I'm tired.
The museum is closed on Mondays. / Ah! Then let's go tomorrow.
Oh! What a surprise! / Hi! I got back yesterday.
See you at eight at the café. / Huh? I didn't hear.
Hey, Marco! How's it going? / Good, and you?
Do you like the movie? / Well, it's not bad.
Where's Luca? / Dunno! I have no idea.
Do you think it'll rain tomorrow? / Hmm! Maybe yes, maybe no.
I don't feel like going out. / Come on, come with us!
I won a hundred euros! / No way! Really?
A cappuccino, please. / Here you are!
One more photo! / Enough, I'm tired!
Shall we go on vacation to Capri? / I wish! But I have no money.
The train is an hour late. / Ugh! How boring!
Ouch! My foot hurts. / Let me see.
Oops! I broke a glass. / Never mind.
There's no school tomorrow! / Hooray!
Darn, I've lost my keys! / Maybe they're in the car?
This bag costs a thousand euros. / Wow! It's too expensive!
Oh my goodness, it's so hot! / Yes, let's go to the beach!
I can't come tonight. / Too bad! Another time, then.
The train arrived on time. / Thank goodness!
Thanks for the help! / Don't mention it!
Can I use the bathroom? / Of course! It's there on the right.
Shall we meet at eight? / OK!
I can't do it anymore! / Come on, you're almost there!
Watch out! There's a car coming! / Thanks!
Achoo! / Bless you!
To our friendship! / Cheers!
Today's my birthday! / Happy birthday!
The restaurant is closed. / Oh well, let's have a pizza at home.
Are you tired? / Not at all! Let's go dancing!
There's a bug in my salad! / Gross! Call the waiter.
